ai_news.title: SubQ Launches First Commercial Subquadratic LLM with 12 Million Token Context Window
ai_news.summary: Startup Subquadratic launched SubQ, the first commercially available LLM built on a fully subquadratic sparse attention architecture, departing from the standard transformer design. The model ships with a native 12-million-token context window and claims roughly one-fifth the cost of frontier models with up to 52x faster performance. The company raised $29 million in seed funding to bring the model to market.
ai_news.relevance: This is a potential paradigm shift away from quadratic-attention transformers, offering a scalable path to massive context windows at a fraction of current inference costs.

ai_news.title: GPT-5.5 Instant Becomes New Default Model for ChatGPT
ai_news.summary: OpenAI replaced its previous default model with GPT-5.5 Instant, rolling it out as the standard experience for ChatGPT users worldwide. The new default is optimized for speed and responsiveness while maintaining strong reasoning capabilities. The move signals OpenAI's continued push to improve everyday user experience alongside its more capable flagship models.
ai_news.relevance: As the model now serving the largest user base in consumer AI, GPT-5.5 Instant's capabilities and limitations will directly shape public perception and enterprise adoption of LLMs.

ai_news.title: Gemini 3.5 Flash Reaches General Availability, Delivers Frontier Intelligence at 4x Speed
ai_news.summary: Google's Gemini 3.5 Flash model is now generally available, offering frontier-level intelligence at four times the speed of comparable models and priced at $1.50/$9 per million tokens with a 1-million-token context window. The model targets production workloads that require both high capability and low latency. Its availability marks a significant step in making high-performance AI accessible at scale.
ai_news.relevance: Combining frontier-class reasoning with sub-second latency and a competitive price point makes Gemini 3.5 Flash a strong candidate for real-time agentic and enterprise AI applications.

ai_news.title: Google Unveils TurboQuant at ICLR 2026, Slashing LLM KV Cache Memory Overhead
ai_news.summary: Google researchers presented TurboQuant at ICLR 2026, an algorithm that significantly reduces the memory burden of the KV cache in large language models through a two-step process combining PolarQuant vector rotation and Quantized Johnson-Lindenstrauss compression. The technique targets one of the primary bottlenecks in long-context LLM inference. It has implications for both training efficiency and deployment cost at scale.
ai_news.relevance: KV cache memory is a major constraint on serving long-context models; TurboQuant's compression approach could substantially reduce GPU memory requirements and inference costs for production deployments.

ai_news.title: Meta Signs $100 Billion AMD Chip Agreement to Diversify AI Infrastructure
ai_news.summary: Meta announced a multiyear agreement to purchase up to $100 billion worth of AMD chips as part of a strategy to diversify its AI hardware supply chain beyond NVIDIA. The deal includes a performance-based warrant giving Meta the option to acquire up to 160 million shares of AMD common stock. The agreement represents one of the largest single AI hardware procurement deals ever announced.
ai_news.relevance: This deal accelerates AMD's competitive position in AI accelerator hardware and signals that hyperscalers are actively reducing dependency on any single chip supplier, reshaping the AI infrastructure market.

sfdc_news.title: Amplitude Brings Global Agent to Slack and Microsoft Teams
sfdc_news.summary: Amplitude updated its Slack and Teams integrations so that sharing an Amplitude chart link now surfaces chart context, AI-generated suggested questions, and a direct entry point to a Global Agent conversation within the preview card. Users can click 'Ask Amplitude AI' to interrogate a chart instantly, mention @Amplitude in any thread for follow-up questions, or open the chart directly in Amplitude — all without leaving their messaging app. The update extends the Global Agent launched in February 2026 into everyday team communication workflows.
sfdc_news.relevance: Amplitude users on Slack or Teams-centric teams can now surface and query product analytics data in-context during discussions, reducing the friction of switching tools for data-driven decisions.

sfdc_news.title: Salesforce Summer '26 Release Announcement: Multi-Agent Orchestration and Slack-First Workflows
sfdc_news.summary: Salesforce announced its Summer '26 product release, rolling out June 15, with Multi-Agent Orchestration in Agentforce as the centrepiece — a primary agent intelligently routes queries to specialist agents using the Atlas Reasoning Engine so customers never repeat themselves across channels. The release also introduces Slack-first sales workflows with proactive Agentforce agents that prospect and manage pipeline, Real-Time Offer Management for personalised promotions, and Retail Execution Dashboards for Tableau Next. Agentforce ARR reached $800 million, up 169% year-over-year.
sfdc_news.relevance: Salesforce Agentforce customers will be able to orchestrate complex, multi-department AI workflows through a single intelligent entry point, eliminating context loss between specialist agents.

sfdc_news.title: Salesforce Launches Agentforce Operations to End Back-Office Bottlenecks
sfdc_news.summary: Salesforce announced Agentforce Operations, a product that enables AI agents to automate complex, cross-system back-office workflows spanning ERP, ITSM, and other legacy platforms that have historically blocked enterprise AI at the operational layer. The generally available release includes native integrations with existing Salesforce Flows, with deeper auto-sync and trigger capabilities entering beta in May 2026. The product targets the gap between front-office AI wins and back-office execution.
sfdc_news.relevance: Enterprise Salesforce customers can now extend Agentforce beyond CRM into back-office systems, enabling true end-to-end automation of business processes without manual handoffs.

sfdc_news.title: Braze Delivers Agentic AI Capabilities: BrazeAI Operator, Agent Console, and Creative Studio
sfdc_news.summary: Braze launched three new products: BrazeAI Operator, an in-dashboard AI assistant that builds campaigns, creates custom agents, and troubleshoots workflows in natural language; BrazeAI Agent Console, a centralised hub to build and deploy AI agents that generate content, interpret customer data, and adapt campaigns in real time; and Braze Creative Studio, which links asset management and brand templates directly to live campaigns via Figma and Canva integrations. EU hosting on Google Cloud for BrazeAI Decisioning Studio was also added. Early customer results include an 81% reduction in unsubscribes and a 284% increase in app opens.
sfdc_news.relevance: Braze customers can now automate campaign creation, real-time personalisation, and creative asset workflows end-to-end from within a single platform, significantly reducing reliance on technical teams.

sfdc_news.title: Amplitude Introduces Agentic AI Analytics for the Next Era of Product Experiences
sfdc_news.summary: Amplitude announced a suite of AI agents natively embedded in its analytics platform, including a Global Agent for natural-language querying across funnels, experiments, segments, and customer journeys, plus four specialised agents for deeper analysis. The launch included MCP integrations connecting Amplitude behavioural data to third-party tools including Anthropic, OpenAI, Cursor, Figma, Lovable, Notion, and GitHub, enabling analytics context to flow into existing development and design workflows. Unlike generic AI tools querying a data warehouse, Amplitude's agents are purpose-built to understand behavioural context.
sfdc_news.relevance: Product and data teams using Amplitude can now ask complex analytical questions in plain language and receive actionable insights instantly, while feeding behavioural context directly into their broader AI-powered toolchain.

claude_news.title: Anthropic Opens Seoul Office, Appoints KiYoung Choi as Korea Representative Director
claude_news.summary: Anthropic appointed KiYoung Choi as Representative Director of Korea and opened a Seoul office on May 26, 2026. The move signals Anthropic's continued international expansion into the Asia-Pacific region. This makes Korea one of Anthropic's newest regional headquarters outside the US.
claude_news.relevance: Marks Anthropic's formal entry into the South Korean market, expanding Claude's availability and enterprise support in Asia.

claude_news.title: Anthropic's Code with Claude Showed Off Coding's Future—Whether You Like It or Not
claude_news.summary: Anthropic held its first developer-focused event in Europe, 'Code with Claude,' in East London. The event showcased the future of AI-assisted software development and featured commentary on AI safety. The event coincided with reports of Anthropic raising funds at a $900 billion valuation.
claude_news.relevance: Signals how Anthropic is positioning Claude Code as the future of software development and expanding its developer community in Europe.

claude_news.title: Anthropic Forms $200 Million Partnership with the Gates Foundation
claude_news.summary: Anthropic announced a $200 million partnership with the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, combining grant funding, Claude usage credits, and technical support. The initiative targets global health, life sciences, education, and economic mobility over the next four years. This is Anthropic's largest philanthropic-focused partnership to date.
claude_news.relevance: Expands Claude's application into global development and humanitarian sectors, with significant resources directed toward high-impact social problems.

claude_news.title: KPMG Integrates Claude Across Its Core Business
claude_news.summary: KPMG announced a global alliance with Anthropic to embed Claude into its Digital Gateway software platform and make it accessible to all 276,000+ employees worldwide. The partnership represents one of the largest enterprise Claude deployments to date. Claude will be used across KPMG's consulting, audit, and advisory services.
claude_news.relevance: One of the biggest enterprise rollouts of Claude to date, demonstrating the model's readiness for large-scale professional services use.

claude_news.title: SAP and Anthropic to Bring Claude to SAP Business AI Platform
claude_news.summary: SAP and Anthropic announced a partnership to make Claude a primary reasoning and agentic AI capability embedded across SAP's AI-enabled solution portfolio. Claude will be integrated into SAP's newly announced Business AI Platform for enterprise customers globally. The deal positions Claude as a core engine for enterprise resource planning and business operations AI.
claude_news.relevance: Embeds Claude into one of the world's most widely used enterprise software ecosystems, reaching millions of SAP business customers.
